hints.text: Launches into the air and crashes down on the player's position
The landing releases a spread of projectiles fanning outward
Between big leaps, makes small hops toward the player to close distance
Standing behind the landing point after its jump avoids the burst entirely
Its entire moveset: small hops to close in, then an off-screen leap aimed at the player — nothing else
A grotesque mouth-shaped creature; one of the first bosses of the Basement
Chases the player around the room with no projectile attacks
Randomly drops poop while moving, cluttering the room with obstacles
Its body is composed of multiple segments, each with its own HP
Hitting the body at the right junction can split it into two independent enemies
Each split-off piece continues chasing independently — one threat becomes several
A segmented worm from the Basement; multiple copies can be present in a fight from the start
Hovers diagonally around the room, never touching the floor
Periodically coughs up Attack Flies
The spawned flies orbit around it, physically blocking the player's shots
Once enough flies accumulate, sends them all out to chase the player
Has no direct attacks — relies entirely on its fly entourage for offense
A bloated fly-boss from the Basement; its living projectile-shield makes safe targeting difficult
One body pursues the player and periodically rushes at increased speed
A smaller second body fires projectiles at the player while tethered
The fight changes based on which of the two bodies is killed first
If the small body detaches, it charges furiously with high momentum
Killing the large body first leaves only the fast-charging small body
A conjoined twin boss from the Basement — two bodies, one fight
Spends most of the fight underground, surfacing only to strike
Launches toward the player's position when leaping out of the ground
Longer leaps fire diagonal projectiles on takeoff and mid-air
Can partially surface to fire a single red Ipecac shot before diving back under
Only briefly vulnerable during and immediately after surfacing
A worm-like boss that stays burrowed between attacks; one of the most widely-distributed bosses in the game
Charges across the room at high speed
Spawns flies throughout the fight
Loses its lower body at half health, fundamentally changing how it moves
In phase two the severed head makes repeated horizontal charge passes
The charging head also spits shots at the player during its passes
First of the four Horsemen — a gaunt rider whose horse is destroyed midway through the fight
Periodically oozes yellow creep puddles that deal contact damage
Fires a burst of 8 projectiles outward in all directions
Leaps toward the player and fires a ring of 12 projectiles on landing
Loses a body part at two-thirds and one-third HP — gone permanently
Detached parts bounce diagonally off walls forever, invulnerable, dealing contact damage — they do not fire
A bloated creature from the Caves; its popping eyes and floor creep make the arena increasingly hazardous
Charges in a straight line when aligned cardinally with the player
Spawns Charger enemies throughout the fight
Her own charges can run over and kill the Chargers she spawned
Up to five Chargers can be alive simultaneously
Eats bombs placed in her charge path, briefly stunning herself
A large segmented grub from the Caves; charges and spawned Chargers are her entire toolkit
Makes large leaps across the room toward the player
Leaves a white creep puddle at each landing point
Spawns a Sack on each landing; up to three alive at once
Can spit spiders directly at the player
Every landing simultaneously deposits creep and a new minion — hazards accumulate fast
A spider-like boss; white creep and persistent Sacks define the late-fight arena
Fires a spread of 5 projectiles in a wide arc
Spawns Pooters during the fight
Spawns pairs of weak Attack Flies behind herself
Can direct the spread in multiple directions — but never directly behind herself
Also summons pairs of Boils in front of herself
A large stationary creature anchored to the top of the Caves room — the only boss that never moves
Charges at the player, bouncing off walls and obstacles until losing momentum
Jumps and fires a ring of 8 tears in all directions on landing
Spawns a Pooter during the fight
The charge has high momentum — wall ricochets make the path unpredictable
The jump-and-ring-fire on landing fires 8 simultaneous outward projectiles
A smaller, mobile version of a Caves boss; trades immobility for charge-and-leap aggression
Charges in a straight line when aligned cardinally with the player
Spawns Suckers to assist in the fight
Shrinks continuously as it takes damage — no HP thresholds, just constant escalation
The smaller it gets, the faster and more frequent its charges become
Eats bombs placed in its charge path, briefly stunning itself
A large creature from the Caves similar to another boss; uniquely, dealing damage actively makes it more dangerous
Flies diagonally around the room, bouncing off walls
Occasionally drops poop while moving, cluttering the arena
Splits into smaller copies when its segments take damage
Multiple independent copies can be active in a single fight
No projectile attacks — all danger is contact with an accumulating number of flying worms
A skeletal flying worm — the undead counterpart of a Basement boss, found in the Catacombs
Fires a horizontal Brimstone beam when the player is to its left or right
Leaps off-screen and lands on the player's position twice in a row
First landing fires 8 projectiles outward in all directions
Second landing spawns Suckers
Also hops toward the player between off-screen leaps
A larger, angrier version of a Basement boss — same leap pattern, now with a Brimstone laser, found in the Depths
Fires an arcing black Ipecac shot that leaves a large black creep puddle on impact
Leaps off-screen and lands on the player's position twice in a row
First landing creates a large black creep puddle that persists for the entire fight
Second landing spawns Clots
Also makes short hops toward the player between off-screen leaps
A tar-like creature from the Depths; covers the floor with permanent black creep, making the arena shrink over time
A giant foot descends from the ceiling and slams down on the player's position
A hand reaches in from a doorway to deal contact damage
An eye pokes out from a doorway — it does not fire, but deals contact damage
A piece of flesh extends from a doorway and spawns an enemy into the room
Foot, hand, eye, and flesh attacks can arrive from different walls in rapid succession
Only her limbs and eye are ever visible — she operates the entire room as her arena
Periodically summons waves of powerful minions and becomes invulnerable until every one is killed
Three separate invulnerable summon phases trigger as its HP depletes
Slams its fists into the ground to create expanding rings of fissures
Slams its head down to launch a wide barrage of mortar-style tears
Once its full HP pool is gone, transforms into a skull that vomits flames, zigzagging tears, and splitting projectiles
The secret final boss — requires a specific key to open the giant golden door at the end of The Chest or The Dark Room
Floats around the room leaving a continuous trail of damaging green creep
Fires Ipecac-style shots that leave additional green creep puddles on impact
Summons Chargers and Spitties during the fight (up to four at once)
The fight changes at half health — movement slows but projectile rate increases
Second phase spawns Attack Flies instead of ground-based enemies
Second of the four Horsemen — a plague rider whose entire offense revolves around green creep and disease, found in Chapter 2
Charges horizontally across the entire room three times in succession
Fires 8 projectiles outward in all directions
Flies off-screen and drops five Troll Bombs before returning from the side
The mount is destroyed at half health, completely changing how the boss moves
After losing the horse, charges directly at Isaac with increasing speed and ever-tighter turns
Third of the four Horsemen — an armored rider whose horse explodes when it falls, found in Chapter 3
Spawns large projectile weapons along the walls that accelerate toward the player after a brief delay
Also spawns a pair of these weapons that immediately home in on the player
Uses a time-slowing ability that reduces the player's movement speed for a brief window
Dismounts at half health; the horse then continuously charges across the room at three different heights
After dismounting, occasionally spawns armored enemies — the horse keeps charging even after the rider is defeated
Fourth and final Horseman — death personified; his scythes and horse remain threats even after he falls, found in Chapter 4

name: The Fallen
location: Any chapter including Sheol — special boss room

hints.text: Fires a spread of projectiles in succession toward the player
Moves in cardinal directions, pursuing the player between attacks
After taking damage, fires Brimstone lasers in all four cardinal directions simultaneously
At half health, permanently splits into two independent copies
Both copies after the split are fully functional with the same Brimstone and spread attacks
A demonic winged creature that can appear as a special boss in any chapter — its split at half health is its defining trait
Fires disorganized bursts of red projectiles outward, similar to an early-game boss
Releases expanding rings of fire projectiles that rotate as they spread outward
Spits out a Hopper enemy below itself
Can release two rings simultaneously rotating in opposite directions, or a single larger ring
Has no phase changes — the same attacks throughout, with no HP-based escalation
A large stationary creature from the Depths; combines burst fire, rotating flame rings, and a minion
Fires expanding rings of projectiles that rotate clockwise or counter-clockwise
Spawns Leaper enemies that land anywhere in the room and immediately attack
Can fire a ring of 11 projectiles straight outward in all directions simultaneously
Up to four Leapers can be alive at once
When two or more Leapers are alive, charges up and fires a Brimstone laser that bends to connect through each one
A large stationary posthumous creature from the Necropolis — its signature laser hunts the player through its own minions
Leaps off-screen and tries to land near the player, predicting their movement
Landing creates a grey creep puddle and sends out lines of rock waves
Fires multiple streams of projectiles in a spiral pattern
Curls into a ball and charges at the player, bouncing off walls
Spawns a Vis that fires Brimstone lasers
A large rolling creature from the Depths; its predictive leap, spiral fire, and Vis minion combine for a chaotic fight
Fires a Brimstone laser toward the player in any cardinal direction
Flies off-screen and plummets down on the player's position, creating an expanding ring of rock waves on impact
Summons spiders during the fight
The laser bends slightly to follow the player's movement as it fires — harder to dodge at distance
Temporarily dims the room during the fight — a localized darkness effect, not a permanent run curse
A flying demon from the Necropolis — dive-bombing, a tracking laser, and room-darkening define its fight
Floats around the room like a flying boss, but considerably faster
Spawns Attack Flies that orbit it loosely, blocking the player's projectiles
Fires a spray of projectiles outward, similar to a well-known early boss
Also spawns spiders during the fight
Fires blood shots in all 8 directions simultaneously, releasing its orbiting flies to chase the player
A decayed, skeletal flying boss from the Catacombs — the posthumous counterpart of a Chapter 1 boss
Makes large leaps across the room toward the player
Leaves a large white creep puddle at each landing point
Fires a ring of 8 projectiles outward on each landing — unlike its Chapter 2 counterpart
Spawns spiders and larger spider enemies on landing
Every landing simultaneously creates creep, fires a projectile ring, and spawns minions
A skeletal spider-like boss from the Catacombs — a deadlier version of a Chapter 1 alternate boss
Slowly bounces off walls, pursuing the player by contact
Splits into smaller copies when damaged
Undergoes three splitting stages — large into medium, medium into small
Each smaller form moves noticeably faster than the last
The smallest fragments spawn spiders on death, adding persistent hazards at the end of the fight
A blob-like creature from the Womb with no projectile attacks at all — pure contact pressure and spider spawns
Teleports to random positions around the room
Fires coordinated bursts of projectiles in cardinal then diagonal directions
Fires 8 projectiles outward in all directions
Spawns a Red Boom Fly during the fight (only one alive at once)
Consists of two completely independent halves — both act simultaneously, effectively doubling every attack
A twin-form boss from the Womb; killing one half does not affect the other
Fires a ring of 8 projectiles outward in all directions
Fires Brimstone lasers from its eye sockets at the player
Leaps toward the player, leaving red creep and a ring of 8 projectiles on landing
Creates pools of red creep throughout the fight
Has detached eyeballs that bounce diagonally around the room, blocking shots and dealing contact damage
A bloated eyeball-like boss from the Depths and Womb chapters — shares the eye-detachment mechanic of a Chapter 2 boss but adds lasers and red creep
Creates temporary spikes that appear in random locations around the room
Fires waves of spread projectiles toward the player's position
Spews large projectiles that leave slowing orange creep on impact
Retreats off-screen periodically, then returns immediately with another attack
The spread-fire comes in 3, 4, or 7 waves — the count varies, making the pattern unpredictable
A large stationary creature at the top of the Womb room — the largest of a family of Caves bosses, now with spikes and slowing creep
Fires expanding rings of projectiles outward
Spawns waves of standard floor enemies — Eyes, Hosts, Globins, and Swingers
Escalates through four distinct phases as its HP is depleted, each adding new attacks
Periodically retreats upward and becomes invulnerable, firing diagonal rotating projectile lines while out of reach
In its final phase, fires four diagonal Brimstone lasers that rotate around the room
The beating heart encountered at the end of the Womb — one of the game's iconic multi-phase final bosses
Fires expanding rings of projectiles outward
From the very first phase, spawns multi-headed creatures and segmented worms not native to this floor — Polycephalus and Fistula
Escalates through four distinct phases, each adding new attacks as HP drops
Retreats upward periodically, becoming invulnerable, and fires four rotating diagonal lines of red projectiles while hidden
Later phases spawn boss-tier enemies — a segmented worm, a splitting blob, and armored knights
The evolved form of Mom's Heart — appears in the same room only after 11+ victories over its predecessor
The fight begins by spawning a lesser demon flanked by Kamikaze Leeches that must be killed before the main boss descends
Fires two rapid consecutive projectile spreads toward the player in quick succession
Fires two Brimstone lasers simultaneously that curve apart, leaving a navigable gap between them
Also fires a single downward Brimstone beam from its mouth
A later flying form slams the ground at the player's last position — stomps arrive sequentially and persist briefly
The lord of Sheol — a three-stage fight: a demonic herald, a descending statue, and a final flying form
Fires many lines of projectiles outward in all directions simultaneously
Some projectile groups curve back toward the boss after their initial outward travel, creating a double-pass threat
Summons Angelic Babies in pairs during the fight
Calls down diagonal beam strikes at random positions around the room
Grows angelic wings in the final phase and begins dashing toward the player's position
A weeping child in the Cathedral — the penultimate boss of the divine path, reached only with the Polaroid
Fires many rapid lines of projectiles outward that curve as they travel
Fires pairs of projectile lines — one straight, one homing — expanding outward together
Summons flies that orbit it, blocking the player's shots and limiting safe approach angles
Fires repeated volleys of homing projectiles throughout all phases — notably more homing-focused than a similar fight in the Cathedral
Grows wings in the final phase and drifts toward the player while teleporting to intercept movement
A ghostly form in The Chest — the alternate endgame boss to a visually similar fight in the Cathedral
Fires rings of projectiles with one deliberately aimed at the player's current position
Also fires rotating waves of projectiles that split into additional projectiles on contact
Unleashes Ipecac-style bursts of projectiles in random directions throughout the fight
At half health, permanently splits into a head and a body — each half then acts completely independently
After splitting, the head charges directly and repeatedly at the player
The severed head fires Brimstone lasers in all cardinal directions, rotating 90° between shots
Fires rotating rings of projectiles with varying gaps and spacing
Spawns specialized Hush Flies in geometric formations that orbit it, launch at the player, or actively chase
Later phases add dense interlocking rings with specific safe gaps and spiral patterns
Also spawns Blue Gapers and Boils that add persistent floor pressure to an already crowded arena
In its final sub-phase, fires laser beams from its eyes that leave trails of blue creep along the floor
An ancient entity with an enormous health pool — found in a secret floor accessible only by defeating the Womb boss in under 30 minutes
In its base form, fires rings of projectiles in slow expanding rotations
Also fires Ipecac-style projectiles in all directions from its base form
Periodically transforms into other bosses encountered during the run, fully inheriting their attack patterns
Teleports more frequently and attacks faster as its health decreases
The transformation pool draws from most bosses defeated during the current run — but not all categories of bosses are included
A shapeshifting abomination in The Void — the post-endgame boss requiring completion of two separate chapter-6 endings
Fires radial bursts of 8 projectiles; lingering in their auras triggers additional beam strikes
Fires rays that appear harmless for a moment before snapping into lethal lasers — timing the dodge window is key
Also fires a static Brimstone beam that bends to track the player's position
In its second form, charges across the room repeatedly while releasing radial bursts of feather projectiles
Transforms from a TV-attached form into a winged orb resembling an Ophanim when its first form is destroyed
A divine entity in the Home floor — Phase 1 is anchored to a television that must be targeted directly; Phase 2 takes flight
Charges across the side-scrolling arena at the player, pushing the screen forward while stalagmites and stalactites advance from both sides
After inhaling rings of fire, fires a massive Brimstone-like beam covering the bottom and middle portions of the screen
Between charges, releases large rings of fire — each ring has exactly one gap to pass through safely
In Phase 2, roars to summon Beast Souls — spectral forms that chase and charge at the player
In Phase 3, charges indefinitely while stalagmites and stalactites spawn behind every pass
The true final boss of Isaac — fought in a unique side-scrolling lava arena; flight is automatically granted before this encounter begins
Fires trailing waves of projectiles that weave across the arena and eventually home in on the player
Retreats upward periodically, becoming invulnerable, and summons a massive horde of walking enemies that march toward her position
Throws a knife downward that emits horizontal projectiles while traveling, then bursts into a radial spray on hitting the wall
Ground slams simultaneously release projectile streams and spawn Small Maggots
The second phase makes her mobile — she breaks free of the ceiling to actively charge and reposition across the arena
A massive maternal boss from the Corpse — Phase 1 pins her to the ceiling; Phase 2 tears her loose to pursue the player
Spits out Small Leeches that orbit it, physically blocking the player's projectiles
Fires 6 streams of projectiles outward simultaneously in a radial burst
If 6 or more leeches are alive in the room, the boss cannot use any of its attacks — clearing minions is the primary safety tool
Once damaged sufficiently, starts leaping toward the player and firing bursts of arcing projectiles on landing
Below 25% HP, chains 3–5 consecutive jumps while firing in all cardinal and diagonal directions on each landing
A small blue creature from the alt-Chapter 1 floors — accumulating its own minions can paradoxically protect the player
Spends most of the fight in pits underground, surfacing only to attack
Partially emerges from a pit to fire a disorganized spray of projectiles, then submerges again
Lunges from a pit directly toward the player, releasing 4 projectiles in the cardinal directions at the apex of its leap
At 33% HP, repeatedly stabs the ground at the player's position 3–6 times, permanently creating new pits that shrink the safe arena
After the tail strikes, charges horizontally from the wall while spawning 3 Small Leeches
An aquatic worm from the alt-Chapter 1 floors — at low health it permanently digs pits, shrinking the safe arena
In its starting form, summons Wall Creep enemies on the room walls that fire at the player while following them vertically
After losing a third of its HP, transitions to large disorganized projectile bursts similar to Monstro, plus spawning 3–4 Spiders or a Trite
In the final form, slams against the walls to dislodge rock projectiles and spiders from the ceiling
Final form also fires a single wide Brimstone laser with a moderate charge-up time
Can additionally fire four diagonal Brimstone beams simultaneously that converge inward, leaving a safe gap at the center
A giant spider from the Depths — transforms through three named forms (Wall Creep, Blind Creep, Rage Creep), each with a completely different attack set
Armored head segments are immune to all non-explosive damage — only explosives can destroy the rock casing
Armored heads spit Ink projectiles; once armor is destroyed they switch to spitting Suckers instead
Exposed body segments fire bloody projectiles at the player
Roams the room randomly like a segmented worm; becomes progressively faster as more armor is destroyed
Releases small ink-like enemies that clutter the room while the bosses are still shielded
A pair of armored worms from the Mines — their rock armor blocks most damage; only explosives and a handful of special item effects can bypass it
Creates a ring of 12 projectiles around itself and fires them in staggered sequence starting from two opposite ends of the ring
Also creates two horizontal lines of 6 projectiles each on both sides, firing from the outer edges inward at intervals
Summons a large overhead water projectile that pops into a burst of shots in random directions
Follows the player while twirling and accumulating hovering projectiles, then releases them in an 8-way radial burst
Defeating it stops rain that was falling throughout the entire fight
A fluid creature from the alt-Chapter 1 floors — every attack pattern converges on or follows the player's position
